Findings:
[{"id":"f-lol-cap-967127db","ruleId":"LOL-CAP","ruleTitle":"Limitation of liability — cap, mutuality and carve-outs","severity":"critical","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 21.1 Except for Excluded Claims, each Party's total aggregate liability arising out of or relating to this Agreement shall not exceed the greater of the Fees paid or payable by Customer during the twelve months preceding the event giving rise to the claim and USD 1,000,000. The cap is mutual and applies regardless of the form of action or number of claims.","rationale":"Section 21 meets our preferred position. The cap is expressly mutual and set at the greater of 12 months' Fees \"paid or payable\" and USD 1,000,000; \"Fees\" (§1.5) covers recurring subscription, professional services and usage fees, so the base is not illusory. Section 21.2 is a mutual exclusion of indirect/consequential damages (and helpfully confirms restoration, replacement services, notification and incident-response costs are direct damages, which favours us). Section 21.3 carves out, uncapped, breach of confidentiality, data-protection and security obligations, indemnification obligations, gross negligence, wilful misconduct, fraud and infringement of the other Party's IP, and confirms Customer's obligation to pay undisputed Fees is not \"damages\". Section 18.2 further confirms insurance does not limit Vendor's liability. No one-sided or sub-6-month cap and no indemnity inside the cap, so no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-assign-329c36c9","ruleId":"ASSIGN","ruleTitle":"Assignment and change of control","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 24.1 Customer may assign this Agreement or an Order Form without Vendor's consent to an Affiliate or to a successor in a merger, reorganization, acquisition, or sale of all or substantially all assets or business to which the Agreement relates. Customer shall give prompt written notice, and the assignee shall assume the applicable obligations.","rationale":"Section 24 meets our preferred position in full: 24.1 gives Customer a consent-free right to assign to an Affiliate or M&A successor (notice plus assumption only); 24.2 bars Vendor assignment, delegation of material performance, or transfer by change of control without our consent (not unreasonably withheld) and never to a direct competitor; 24.3 applies a reasonable-consent standard to other assignments; and 24.4 expressly denies Vendor any right to terminate, suspend, reprice, accelerate Fees, or reduce service on our change of control. Section 13.3 carries the same carve-out through to licence rights. No change-of-control trigger operates against us elsewhere (9.2 is an ordinary insolvency clause and expressly excludes lawful reorganizations). No redline needed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ld-edb75f99","ruleId":"LD","ruleTitle":"Liquidated damages and penalties payable by Customer","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 27.3 If a force-majeure event materially prevents an affected Service for more than fifteen consecutive days, Customer may procure substitute services and suspend affected Fees. After thirty consecutive days, Customer may terminate the affected Order Form without penalty and receive a refund of prepaid Fees for the unavailable period.","rationale":"The Agreement contains no liquidated damages, penalty, or early-termination/minimum fee payable by Customer. Searches for \"liquidated damages\", \"penalty\", \"early termination\" and \"shall pay\" return only Section 7.1 (ordinary Fees), Section 22.2 (audit costs on a >5% underpayment, a cost-shifting mechanic rather than an LD), and Section 27.3, which expressly lets Customer terminate \"without penalty\". The termination provisions (Sections 9 and 10) impose no exit charge and in fact require Vendor refunds of prepaid Fees. This meets the preferred position, so no redline. Noted but not flagged here: the Section 2.1 take-or-pay commitment of USD 2,000,000 per year \"without reduction or termination rights\" is the closest economic exposure, but it is a minimum-volume commitment addressed under the minimum-commitment rule, not a liquidated damages clause, and we do not flag the same commercial term twice. Also noted: the service-level exhibit referenced in Section 2.2 is not in this document, so we cannot confirm service credits run in our favour.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-license-b9030008","ruleId":"LICENSE","ruleTitle":"Licence grant scope","severity":"high","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 13.1 Subject to payment of applicable Fees, Vendor grants Customer, its Affiliates, and contractors acting on their behalf a worldwide, non-exclusive right during the subscription term to access and use the hosted Services and documentation for their internal business purposes and to provide services to Customer. Customer may permit Authorized Users to exercise those rights.","rationale":"The grant clause meets the preferred position in full. Section 13.1 extends the subscription right to Customer, its Affiliates and contractors acting on their behalf (no notice condition needed); Section 13.2 gives Customer and its Affiliates a perpetual, irrevocable, royalty-free, fully paid licence for delivered/embedded Vendor Technology, including contractor support rights; and Section 13.3 permits transfer to an Affiliate or successor under the Section 24 assignment right and bars revocation or suspension except for a material uncured payment or use breach after notice and a cure opportunity. Nothing makes the licence revocable at Vendor's discretion. Noted but not flagged here: Section 14.2 describes the Deliverable licence as \"revocable, non-transferable\" and term-limited, which sits awkwardly against Sections 13.2–13.3 and 14.3; that point concerns Deliverable ownership and is addressed under the IP rule rather than duplicated here.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-audit-ec7457dd","ruleId":"AUDIT","ruleTitle":"Audit rights against Customer","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 22.1 Vendor may audit Customer's compliance with licence quantities no more than once in any twelve-month period, on at least thirty days' prior written notice, during normal business hours, and in a manner that does not unreasonably disrupt Customer. An audit will be conducted off-site where practicable by an independent auditor bound by confidentiality.","rationale":"Section 22 is the only provision giving Vendor audit/verification rights over Customer (Section 23 \"Records and Customer Assurance\" contains no operative text, and no monitoring or inspection rights appear elsewhere). It meets the preferred position on every material term: frequency limited to once per twelve months; thirty days' prior written notice; normal business hours with no unreasonable disruption; off-site where practicable via an independent auditor bound by confidentiality; Vendor bears cost unless underpayment exceeds five percent; and Vendor and its auditor are expressly barred from direct access to Customer systems, unrelated Customer Data, privileged material, and third-party confidential information. Section 22.3 adds customer-favourable protections (findings are Customer Confidential Information, copy of the final report, finality on payment). No redline needed.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-ip-4d5f6eab","ruleId":"IP","ruleTitle":"Ownership of deliverables and Customer Data","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 14.2 Vendor exclusively owns every Deliverable created for Customer. Customer receives a revocable, non-transferable licence to use a Deliverable only during the applicable Order Form term.","rationale":"Section 14.2 gives Vendor exclusive ownership of every Deliverable created specifically for Customer (as defined in 1.4) and leaves us only a revocable, non-transferable licence limited to the Order Form term. That fails the preferred position (Customer ownership with Vendor assignment) and also fails the fallback, which requires at minimum a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to use and modify Deliverables. Section 14.1 (Customer Data and pre-existing IP) and 14.4 (no joint ownership) are compliant, and 13.2/14.3 give a perpetual paid-up licence to embedded Vendor Technology — but that licence expressly covers Vendor Technology, not the Deliverable itself, so it does not cure 14.2 and in fact sits in tension with it. Redline flips ownership to Customer with an express assignment while preserving Vendor's retained Vendor Technology rights under 14.3.","proposal":"Add fallback clause: Vendor owns generic tools and know-how; Customer gets a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free licence to use, modify, and sublicense Deliverables","verification":"repaired"},{"id":"f-nosolicit-30553066","ruleId":"NOSOLICIT","ruleTitle":"Non-solicitation of employees binding Customer","severity":"medium","status":"deviation","sectionRef":"§ 12.4 Customer shall not solicit, hire, or employ any Vendor employee during the term or for twenty-four months afterward, regardless of how the employee applies.","rationale":"Section 12.4 binds only the Customer and is a true no-hire (\"hire, or employ ... regardless of how the employee applies\"), running 24 months and covering every Vendor employee rather than only personnel involved in the Services, with no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. That is walk-away territory under the rule and fails the fallback on every material term (mutuality, scope, duration, carve-outs, no no-hire). It also conflicts with Section 12.3, which records that Customer has made no no-hire commitment and may hire anyone responding to general recruitment. We propose the minimal edit to reach the fallback: a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs and no no-hire.","proposal":"Narrow one-way 24-month no-hire to a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel involved in the Services, with general-advertising and unsolicited-approach carve-outs.","verification":"fail"},{"id":"f-renewal-efa4e44f","ruleId":"RENEWAL","ruleTitle":"Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice window","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 8.2 Each Order Form has the initial term stated in it and thereafter renews for successive twelve-month periods unless Customer gives Vendor at least thirty days' written notice of non-renewal. Vendor shall remind Customer of an upcoming renewal at least sixty days beforehand. Failure to send the reminder extends Customer's opt-out deadline until thirty days after the reminder is received.","rationale":"Section 8.2 provides automatic renewal for successive twelve-month (not multi-year) periods, with a Customer opt-out on only thirty days' written notice — at the preferred ≤30-day window — plus a Vendor reminder at least sixty days before renewal and an extension of the opt-out deadline if the reminder is not sent, which is better than the preferred reminder mechanic. Section 8.3 caps renewal uplift at the lesser of US CPI-U over the preceding twelve months and three percent, matching the preferred cap, requires ninety days' notice of any increase, and bars increases on prepaid periods. The renewal terms bind Vendor and favour Customer; no redline is warranted.","verification":"pass"},{"id":"f-warranty-f817c2ff","ruleId":"WARRANTY","ruleTitle":"Performance warranty and duration","severity":"medium","status":"compliant","sectionRef":"§ 19.2 For ninety days after delivery or acceptance, whichever is later, each Deliverable will materially conform to its documentation and acceptance criteria. {"markdown":"# Issues Memo — Master Services Agreement

**Prepared for:** Customer (internal)  
**Subject:** Playbook review findings, proposed redlines and walk-away items  
**Findings reviewed:** 18 (10 compliant, 5 deviations, 3 missing)

---

## Executive summary

The ri[REDACTED] core of this Agreement is in good shape. Liability (§ 21), assignment and change of control (§ 24), the licence grant (§ 13), audit rights (§ 22), auto-renewal and price uplift (§ 8), warranties (§ 19) and Vendor insurance (§ 18) all meet our preferred positions, and several provisions are better than our benchmark (mutual cap at the greater of 12 months' Fees paid or payable and USD 1,000,000; hosted-Service conformity for the full subscription term; renewal-reminder mechanic that extends our opt-out deadline; uncapped carve-outs for confidentiality, data protection, security and indemnity).

The problems are concentrated in the commercial-lock-in and exit provisions, and in one significant omission. **There is no indemnification clause at all** — Section 20 is simply absent, even though §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3 and 30.5 all cross-refer to it. Separately, § 2.1 imposes a USD 2,000,000 per year, three-year take-or-pay "without reduction or termination rights"; § 7.2 imposes a disclose-and-match obligation that operates as both de facto exclusivity and a Customer-side MFN; § 12.4 imposes a 24-month one-way no-hire and an undefined-scope non-compete on us; there is no termination-for-convenience right; and there is no transition-assistance or data-return obligation on exit. Section 28.1 selects Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction, which is outside our accepted list and contradicts § 28.2 (New York County courts).

The draft is also internally inconsistent in ways that help us in negotiation: § 12.3 records that Customer has made **no** exclusivity, MFN, minimum-volume, non-compete or no-hire commitment, which directly contradicts §§ 2.1, 7.2 and 12.4. We should press that inconsistency rather than argue each term in isolation. We also note the service-level exhibit referenced in § 2.2 is not in the document (so we cannot confirm service credits run in our favour), no Section 11 exists despite the cross-reference in § 16.5, and § 14.2's "revocable, non-transferable" Deliverable licence sits awkwardly against §§ 13.2–13.3 and 14.3.

---

## Findings

| Severity | Rule | Status | Section | Note |
|---|---|---|---|---|
| Critical | LOL-CAP — Limitation of liability: cap, mutuality, carve-outs | Compliant | § 21.1 (with §§ 21.2, 21.3, 18.2) | Meets preferred position; mutual cap, uncapped Excluded Claims. No redline. |
| High | ASSIGN — Assignment and change of control | Compliant | § 24.1 (with §§ 24.2–24.4, 13.3) | Meets preferred position in full; no change-of-control trigger against us. |
| High | LD — Liquidated damages / penalties payable by Customer | Compliant | § 27.3 | No LD, penalty or exit charge; § 27.3 terminates "without penalty". § 2.1 exposure handled under MINCOMMIT. |
| High | LICENSE — Licence grant scope | Compliant | § 13.1 (with §§ 13.2–13.3) | Meets preferred position; § 14.2 tension addressed under IP. |
| Medium | AUDIT — Audit rights against Customer | Compliant | § 22.1 (with §§ 22.2–22.3) | Meets preferred position on every material term. |
| Medium | IP — Ownership of Deliverables and Customer Data | **Deviation** | § 14.2 | Vendor owns all Deliverables; we get only a revocable, term-limited licence. Fails the fallback. |
| Medium | NOSOLICIT — Non-solicitation binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 | One-way 24-month no-hire of any Vendor employee, no carve-outs. Walk-away territory. |
| Medium | RENEWAL — Auto-renewal and non-renewal notice | Compliant | § 8.2 (with § 8.3) | 12-month renewals, 30-day opt-out, CPI/3% uplift cap. Better than preferred on reminders. |
| Medium | WARRANTY — Performance warranty and duration | Compliant | § 19.2 (with §§ 19.1, 19.3–19.5) | Meets or exceeds preferred; disclaimer limited to implied warranties. |
| Low | EXCLUSIVITY — Exclusivity binding Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 | De facto exclusivity/ROFR across all Services for the full term, no performance exit. Walk-away territory. |
| Low | GOVLAW — Governing law and venue | **Deviation** | § 28.1 | Singapore law and exclusive Singapore jurisdiction; outside accepted list and conflicts with § 28.2. Walk-away territory. |
| Low | INDEMN — Indemnification by Vendor | **Missing** | No Section 20 in document (see § 19.5; cross-refs at §§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3, 30.5) | No Vendor IP or other indemnity anywhere. Walk-away territory. |
| Low | INSURANCE — Vendor insurance | Compliant | § 18 (with § 18.2) | CGL, E&O, USD 5M cyber/privacy, workers' comp; term plus one year. |
| Low | MFN — Most-favoured-nation burdening Customer | **Deviation** | § 7.2 | Open-ended Customer-side disclose-and-match duty; no product, duration or comparability limits. Walk-away territory. |
| Low | MINCOMMIT — Minimum purchase commitments | **Deviation** | § 2.1 | USD 2,000,000/year for three years, take-or-pay, "without reduction or termination rights". Walk-away territory. |
| Low | NONCOMPETE — Non-compete restrictions on Customer | **Deviation** | § 12.4 | Term plus 24 months, "any product or service", "any territory", no carve-outs. Walk-away territory. |
| Low | T4C — Termination for convenience | **Missing** | § 9 (§ 9.3 quoted); § 2.1 | No Customer convenience right in a three-year term locked by § 2.1. Walk-away territory. |
| Low | TRANSITION — Transition assistance and data return | **Missing** | § 10.2 (with § 16.5) | No migration assistance, data export or certified deletion; § 16.5 defers to a non-existent Section 11. |

---

## Walk-away items

These sit in walk-away territory under the playbook and, unless resolved, should not be signed:

1. **No indemnification (absent Section 20).** No Vendor IP infringement indemnity or any other defence obligation. We propose inserting a new Section 20 at the preferred position: Vendor defence and indemnity for third-party IP infringement, breach of Applicable Law, Vendor-caused Customer Data breaches and gross negligence/wilful misconduct; standard notice, control and cooperation procedure; customary exclusions and procure–modify–replace–refund remedies at 20.5 (which also cures the dangling cross-reference in § 9.3); and a narrow Customer indemnity limited to Customer-provided content and our breach of law. No super-cap is needed because § 21.3 already treats indemnification obligations as Excluded Claims.
2. **§ 2.1 take-or-pay (MINCOMMIT).** A three-year, USD 2,000,000 per year commitment with no reduction or termination rights. We propose payment only for Services ordered or used; the fallback (a commitment for the current 12-month term only, reducible on 30 days' notice and trued up rather than penalised) is available if Vendor needs a floor.
3. **§ 7.2 disclose-and-match (EXCLUSIVITY and MFN).** Independently breaches both rules: it is an exclusivity/ROFR on our sourcing and an open-ended Customer-side MFN. Preferred remedy is deletion of the Customer-side obligation; any Vendor-granted MFN in our favour would be retained.
4. **§ 12.4 non-compete (NONCOMPETE).** Term plus 24 months, undefined scope and territory, no carve-out for internal development or acquisitions. Preferred remedy is deletion; a narrowed fallback can be offered in comment.
5. **§ 12.4 no-hire (NOSOLICIT).** One-way, 24 months, all Vendor employees, no general-advertising or unsolicited-approach carve-out. Fallback is a mutual 12-month non-solicit limited to personnel directly involved in the Services, with those carve-outs and no no-hire element.
6. **§ 28.1 Singapore law and exclusive Singapore venue (GOVLAW).** Outside the accepted list and in conflict with § 28.2. We propose New York law and the state and federal courts in New York County; § 28.3's pre-suit escalation preserving urgent relief is unaffected.
7. **No termination for convenience (T4C).** No Customer convenience right in a multi-year term expressly locked by § 2.1. We propose a new § 9.4 giving Customer 30 days' notice convenience termination with pro-rata refund of prepaid Fees, and a conforming carve-out in § 2.1 so the right is effective. Vendor likewise has no convenience right, which is consistent with our position.

---

## Next steps

1. **Issue the redline** covering the five deviations and three gaps above. Two proposed edits did not pass automated verification and require manual drafting before the redline goes out: the **§ 12.4 non-solicit narrowing** and the **new § 9.4 convenience-termination right** (including the conforming § 2.1 carve-out).
2. **Lead with the § 12.3 inconsistency.** Vendor's own acknowledgement that Customer has made no exclusivity, MFN, minimum-volume, non-compete or no-hire commitment contradicts §§ 2.1, 7.2 and 12.4. Framing these as drafting conflicts to be conformed to § 12.3 is a cleaner path than five separate commercial negotiations.
3. **Fix the missing and dangling references.** Confirm whether an indemnity was intended and dropped in assembly (§§ 9.3, 19.4, 21.3, 30.5 all assume one), and resolve § 16.5's reference to a non-existent Section 11.
4. **Request the missing service-level exhibit** referenced in § 2.2 so we can confirm service credits and the § 9.3 "repeatedly misses a critical service level" trigger operate in our favour.
5. **Deliverables ownership (§ 14.2).** Seek Customer ownership with an express Vendor assignment, preserving Vendor's retained Vendor Technology rights under § 14.3; the fallback is a perpetual, irrevocable, worldwide, royalty-free, sublicensable licence to use and modify Deliverables. Note the tension with §§ 13.2–13.3 and 14.3, which currently cover Vendor Technology only and do not cure § 14.2.
6. **Add exit protections (new § 10.3):** up to six months' transition assistance at then-current rates, return of Customer Data in a standard machine-readable format within 30 days of expiry or termination, and certified deletion thereafter, with a routine-backup and legal-retention carve-out consistent with § 16.5.
7. **Do not reopen the compliant provisions.** Sections 8, 13, 18, 19, 21, 22 and 24 meet our positions or better; raising them risks trading away favourable terms."}
